uvod: SPOCK is an AI assistant in VS Code. It guides a product team from a first idea to an initiative that is ready to build.
Let's walk through a finished sample run. The customer does not know which recurring payments leave their account.
In every stage, an agent prepares a document, a check verifies it, and a person decides.
faze-1: Stage one, the brief. You start the run yourself with a task. You enter the run name, your name and your role.
The Product Manager agent interviews you and writes the brief. The target state is a change for the customer, not a solution.
The agent asks about one field at a time. It never fills in anything on its own.
What you do not know is recorded as unknown, with a reason. That is an honest brief, not a mistake.
The agent runs the check and fixes what it found. Then you approve the brief, under your own name.
faze-2: Stage two. It does not start without your material. Put the files into the supplied folder. They do not belong in the chat.
The agent extracts observations from the material and frames opportunities: customer needs, not solutions.
Each one carries a trust tag. Strong means at least two independent sources, and one of them first hand.
Weakly supported opportunities stay on the record. Nothing is thrown away.
You decide which opportunities are primary. The agent only proposes the order.
faze-3: Stage three, the market. The agent works from a market file that you prepare. It is the only agent allowed to reach the web.
Each organisation gets a profile: what it offers, how it differs, and what it is confirmed not to do.
The synthesis says what the market already does about your opportunities, so stage four does not guess.
Note: nobody signs stage three. The check accepts it, and you read the result in stage four.
faze-4: Stage four. Only now do solutions appear. The agent proposes several, each built on a different combination of opportunities.
The solutions have no score and no ranking. The agent does not recommend any of them.
For each one you see its regulatory touchpoints. SPOCK does not rate technical complexity, so ask your engineer.
Here, solution I 2 was chosen: a notification before the next payment.
Choosing takes two tasks: you record the choice with your reason, then you approve. The reason is carried forward word for word.
faze-5: Stage five shrinks the chosen solution into something you can pilot.
The agent proposes three options. They differ in how the solution is built. You can add up to three of your own.
You choose the option, and the agent expands only that one. It adds nothing new to it.
You decide twice: first you choose the option, then you accept its expansion.
faze-6: Stage six. The Business Analyst combines six inputs into one document: the P R D.
Every requirement names the measure it serves. A requirement with no measure is visible right away.
The agreed P R D is a separate document. It is created word for word from the draft, when you mark it with a task.
Review the P R D with the whole trio. SPOCK does not judge technical feasibility or cost.
faze-7: Stage seven writes the document the bank actually receives: the initiative, in the Guild's template.
It reads only the agreed P R D. It invents nothing new.
The agent never makes up a Jira key. You enter it yourself with a task, or you write: none yet.
With the G 7 sign-off, the run is complete. You move the initiative into Jira yourself.
zaver: Seven stages, six sign-offs. From the initiative you can trace your way back to a sentence in the original material.
SPOCK does not decide for you. It prepares the groundwork and makes sure nothing came out of nowhere.
Now try it in VS Code, on a run of your own.
